checks.title: Objective lens against body width
checks.summary: The claimed 50 mm objective lens fits within the listed body width of 60 mm.

steps.label: Body width available to the lens
steps.text: Body width available to the lens: 60 mm (the second-longest listed side)

steps.label: Body width with the rounding tolerance
steps.text: Body width with the rounding tolerance: 60 mm × 1.03 = 61.8 mm

assumptions: The objective lens faces along the longest side of the body, so it has to fit within the other two sides. The second-longest listed side is used as the width, which is the most lenient.
Listed dimensions are treated as rounded: a lens up to 3% wider than the listed width passes. This tolerance is a team choice, not a physical constant.
The listed dimensions are taken to describe the monocular itself, as the listing states. Because listed dimensions can be wrong, exceeding this bound is reported as a flag, not a hard result.

checks.summary: Not assessed. The listing states no separate 'actual' magnification or objective size to compare with the headline.
